newsitem.title: UK: EMI tumbles amid Musicland worries.
newsitem.headline: EMI tumbles amid Musicland worries.

text.p: Shares in EMI Plc tumbled on Thursday as analysts at Panmure Gordon highlighted the exposure on the company to the U.S. market and negative implications of troubles at retailer Musicland, dealers said.
The stock was down 47-1/2p at 12.31 stg by 1115 GMT.

Yesterday Musicland asked major record labels including EMI for concessions on payments while it seeks a cash infusion. "We're working hard to improve our financial condition without filing Chapter 11," said a spokeswoman for the company.

The 750-store chain asked labels to accept a deferral of payments, with an option to convert amounts due into equity in the company, although sources in the U.S. said labels were not interested in taking an equity stake.
Analysts at Panmure said they had commented on the Musicland issue but pointed out that EMI was less exposed to the U.S. market than other leading music publishers.
They added that the consolidation of U.S. music retailing had anyway been going on for some time.

"EMI is relatively unexposed to the U.S. market," said Panmure analyst Anthony de Larrinaga. "And this is not a new feature of the market. The consolidation of the U.S. music retail market is not new."
Traders said other brokerages as well as Panmure had earlier commented on the Musicland situation and the possible implications for EMI and other music publishers.

They said EMI may have also been unsettled by results from WH Smith Plc on Wednesday, showing the company's music division Virgin Our Price fell into a 1.4 million stg loss on sales down two percent at 194 million stg.
